spec.description: Ships a day through the 28 straits and canals the IMF follows, from AIS, against the BLS deep sea freight index: the Red Sea detour around the Cape of Good Hope, and what ocean freight costs since.

options.content:
### Shipping through the world's chokepoints, and what ocean freight costs

How many ships pass, day by day, through the 28 straits and canals that world trade funnels through, and
what carriers charge to move it. Since the attacks on ships in the Red Sea began in November 2023, much of
the traffic between Asia and Europe has left **Suez and Bab el-Mandeb** to sail around the **Cape of Good
Hope**, two weeks longer; the freight index shows what that costs.

The **map** sizes each chokepoint by its ships a day over the time range and colours it by the change
against 2023 before the attacks (1 January to 18 November): warm for fewer ships, cool for more. **Hover**
a chokepoint for its traffic week by week; **click** it, or pick it above, for its ships by type below.

Data: [IMF PortWatch](https://portwatch.imf.org) daily chokepoint transits, estimated from AIS, updated
weekly. Freight: BLS producer price index for deep sea freight transportation
([PCU483111483111](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/PCU483111483111), June 1988 = 100, monthly) through
FRED: what US carriers charge, an index, not a spot rate per container. Lanes:
[Global Shipping Lanes](https://github.com/newzealandpaul/Shipping-Lanes) v1 (CC BY 4.0), from the CIA
Map of the World Oceans.

spec.rawSql:
-- Ships a day over the range against 2023 up to 18 November, the last day
-- before the attacks in the Red Sea, at the four passages the detour moved
-- traffic between. In percent.
WITH r AS (
  SELECT portid,
         avg(ships) FILTER (WHERE $__timeFilter(time)) AS now,
         avg(ships) FILTER (WHERE time >= '2023-01-01' AND time < '2023-11-19') AS before
  FROM $transits
  WHERE portid IN ('chokepoint1', 'chokepoint4', 'chokepoint7', 'chokepoint2')
  GROUP BY portid
)
SELECT
  max(CASE WHEN portid = 'chokepoint1' THEN 100 * (now / before - 1) END) AS "Suez Canal",
  max(CASE WHEN portid = 'chokepoint4' THEN 100 * (now / before - 1) END) AS "Bab el-Mandeb",
  max(CASE WHEN portid = 'chokepoint7' THEN 100 * (now / before - 1) END) AS "Cape of Good Hope",
  max(CASE WHEN portid = 'chokepoint2' THEN 100 * (now / before - 1) END) AS "Panama Canal"
FROM r

spec.description: Average ships a day through each passage over the time range, as a change against its average from 1 January to 18 November 2023.
spec.title: Ships a day over the range, against 2023 before the attacks

spec.rawSql:
-- The latest month of the freight index in the range, and how far it stands
-- above its 2023 average, before the Red Sea attacks.
WITH m AS (SELECT max(time) AS t FROM $freight WHERE $__timeFilter(time)),
b AS (SELECT avg(freight_index) AS v FROM $freight WHERE year(time) = 2023)
SELECT f.freight_index AS "Deep sea freight index",
       100 * (f.freight_index / b.v - 1) AS "Against 2023"
FROM m JOIN $freight f ON f.time = m.t, b

spec.description: BLS producer price index for deep sea freight transportation (June 1988 = 100), the latest month in the time range, and how far it stands above its 2023 average.
spec.title: Deep sea freight, latest month

spec.rawSql:
-- One circle per chokepoint: ships a day over the range, sized; the change
-- against 2023 before the Red Sea attacks (1 January to 18 November),
-- coloured. Click one to pick it.
WITH r AS (
  SELECT portid,
         avg(ships) FILTER (WHERE $__timeFilter(time)) AS now,
         avg(ships) FILTER (WHERE time >= '2023-01-01' AND time < '2023-11-19') AS before,
         avg(capacity_t) FILTER (WHERE $__timeFilter(time)) AS tonnes
  FROM $transits GROUP BY portid
)
SELECT c.portid, c.chokepoint, c.latitude, c.longitude,
       round(r.now, 1) AS ships_a_day,
       round(100 * (r.now / r.before - 1), 1) AS change_pct,
       round(r.tonnes / 1e6, 2) AS million_dwt_a_day,
       c.top_goods
FROM $chokepoints c JOIN r USING (portid)
WHERE r.now IS NOT NULL

-- Ships a day, week by week over the range, for the cards on the map: one
-- line per chokepoint, shown on hover.
SELECT $__timeGroup(t.time, '1w') AS time, c.chokepoint, c.latitude, c.longitude,
       round(avg(t.ships), 1) AS ships_a_day
FROM $transits t JOIN $chokepoints c USING (portid)
WHERE $__timeFilter(t.time)
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY time

-- The shipping lanes, Major brightest.
SELECT lane, geometry AS geom FROM $lanes

spec.rawSql:
-- Ships a day, week by week: through Suez and Bab el-Mandeb, the Red Sea
-- route, and around the Cape of Good Hope instead.
SELECT $__timeGroup(time, '1w') AS time,
       avg(ships) FILTER (WHERE portid = 'chokepoint1') AS "Suez Canal",
       avg(ships) FILTER (WHERE portid = 'chokepoint4') AS "Bab el-Mandeb",
       avg(ships) FILTER (WHERE portid = 'chokepoint7') AS "Cape of Good Hope"
FROM $transits
WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND portid IN ('chokepoint1', 'chokepoint4', 'chokepoint7')
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

spec.description: Ships a day, averaged week by week, through Suez and Bab el-Mandeb, the Red Sea route between Asia and Europe, and around the Cape of Good Hope.
spec.title: Around Africa instead of through the Red Sea — ships a day, weekly

spec.rawSql:
-- Month by month: the deep sea freight index, on the right axis, against the
-- ships a day through Suez and around the Cape.
WITH t AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', time) AS time,
         avg(ships) FILTER (WHERE portid = 'chokepoint1') AS suez,
         avg(ships) FILTER (WHERE portid = 'chokepoint7') AS cape
  FROM $transits
  WHERE portid IN ('chokepoint1', 'chokepoint7')
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT f.time, f.freight_index AS "Deep sea freight index",
       t.suez AS "Suez Canal, ships a day", t.cape AS "Cape of Good Hope, ships a day"
FROM $freight f LEFT JOIN t USING (time)
WHERE $__timeFilter(f.time)
ORDER BY 1

spec.rawSql:
-- The picked chokepoint, ships a day by type, week by week.
SELECT $__timeGroup(time, '1w') AS time,
       avg(tanker) AS "Tanker", avg(container) AS "Container", avg(dry_bulk) AS "Dry bulk",
       avg(general_cargo) AS "General cargo", avg(roro) AS "Ro-ro"
FROM $transits
WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND portid = '${chokepoint}'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

spec.rawSql:
-- Every chokepoint over the range: traffic, its change against 2023 before
-- the Red Sea attacks, the tonnage and the share of tankers and container
-- ships. portid feeds the link that picks a row, and stays hidden.
WITH r AS (
  SELECT portid,
         avg(ships) FILTER (WHERE $__timeFilter(time)) AS now,
         avg(ships) FILTER (WHERE time >= '2023-01-01' AND time < '2023-11-19') AS before,
         avg(capacity_t) FILTER (WHERE $__timeFilter(time)) AS tonnes,
         sum(tanker) FILTER (WHERE $__timeFilter(time)) AS tanker,
         sum(container) FILTER (WHERE $__timeFilter(time)) AS container,
         sum(ships) FILTER (WHERE $__timeFilter(time)) AS ships
  FROM $transits GROUP BY portid
)
SELECT c.portid, c.chokepoint AS "Chokepoint",
       r.now AS "Ships a day",
       100 * (r.now / r.before - 1) AS "Against 2023",
       r.tonnes / 1e6 AS "Million dwt a day",
       100 * r.tanker / r.ships AS "Tankers",
       100 * r.container / r.ships AS "Container ships",
       c.top_goods AS "Main goods"
FROM $chokepoints c JOIN r USING (portid)
WHERE r.now IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY r.now DESC

query.rawSql:
-- Server side, once per visit: ships through the 28 chokepoints the IMF's
-- PortWatch follows, counted from AIS, one row per chokepoint and day since
-- 2019. Read through the gateway's day-long cache of the weekly CSV. Counts
-- by vessel type; capacity is the deadweight tonnage that went through.
SELECT strptime(date, '%Y/%m/%d') AS time, portid, portname AS chokepoint,
       n_total::INTEGER AS ships, n_container::INTEGER AS container,
       n_dry_bulk::INTEGER AS dry_bulk, n_general_cargo::INTEGER AS general_cargo,
       n_roro::INTEGER AS roro, n_tanker::INTEGER AS tanker,
       capacity::DOUBLE AS capacity_t
FROM read_csv('http://feeds/portwatch/items/3da2b9ca97684916b75c4013f95d18ab.csv', types = {'date': 'VARCHAR'})

-- Server side, once per visit: where each chokepoint is, and the three kinds
-- of goods PortWatch estimates go through it most. 28 rows.
SELECT portid, portname AS chokepoint, lat::DOUBLE AS latitude, lon::DOUBLE AS longitude,
       nullif(concat_ws(', ', industry_top1, industry_top2, industry_top3), '') AS top_goods
FROM (
  SELECT unnest(features, recursive := true)
  FROM read_json('https://services9.arcgis.com/weJ1QsnbMYJlCHdG/arcgis/rest/services/PortWatch_chokepoints_database/FeatureServer/0/query?where=1%3D1&outFields=portid,portname,lat,lon,industry_top1,industry_top2,industry_top3&returnGeometry=false&f=json')
)

-- Server side, once per visit: the world shipping lanes, Major, Middle and
-- Minor, georeferenced from the CIA Map of the World Oceans (Shipping-Lanes
-- v1, CC BY 4.0). Simplified to about 5 km: some 160 kB for the browser.
SELECT "Type" AS lane,
       ST_AsGeoJSON(ST_SimplifyPreserveTopology(geom, 0.05))::VARCHAR AS geometry
FROM ST_Read('/vsicurl/https://raw.githubusercontent.com/newzealandpaul/Shipping-Lanes/b0ad85cdab959b84bc915b21d77d18bb8f1429f4/data/Shipping_Lanes_v1.geojson')

-- Server side, once per visit: what US carriers charge for deep sea freight,
-- the BLS producer price index PCU483111483111 (June 1988 = 100), monthly,
-- from FRED through the gateway, which adds the API key.
SELECT o.date::TIMESTAMP AS time, try_cast(o.value AS DOUBLE) AS freight_index
FROM (SELECT unnest(observations) AS o FROM read_json('http://feeds/fred/series/PCU483111483111'))
WHERE try_cast(o.value AS DOUBLE) IS NOT NULL
